@malhashemi — appreciate the follow-up, and credit to you for building the permission system (I can see you authored the Task/Skill permission filtering in #5930, #6000, #7042, #7165, #8111). It works, and we use it.

The point of this PR isn't that the functionality is missing — it's that the DX for the common case is unnecessarily verbose. We acknowledged this in the January thread above, but the ergonomics argument hasn't been addressed:

**14 agents × 15 subagents average. Current approach:**

```json
"permission": {
  "task": {
    "*": "deny",
    "subagent-a": "allow",
    "subagent-b": "allow",
    "subagent-c": "allow"
  }
}
```

That's 3 lines of boilerplate per entry (`"name": "allow"`) plus the `"*": "deny"` preamble, repeated across every agent. For our setup that's ~210 permission entries across 14 agents.

**Proposed:**

```json
"subagents": ["subagent-a", "subagent-b", "subagent-c"]
```

Same result. One line. The implementation can be syntactic sugar that generates `permission.task` rules internally — your permission system stays as the source of truth.

This is the same pattern as `includeTools` in MCP server config (#7399) — an allowlist shorthand for a common filtering need. Happy to hear counterarguments on why the verbosity is preferable, but "it already works" doesn't address the DX case being made here.

@rekram1-node @thdxr — would value a maintainer perspective on whether a shorthand is worth adding.

This issue is distinct from both #7273 and #1168.

**#7273** is about the terminal's *own* URL detection being broken by line wrapping — a terminal-side problem where the terminal tries to pattern-match URLs in the visible text but fails when the URL wraps.

**#1168** is a feature request for Ctrl+Click support.

**This issue (#14966)** is about **opencode's tree-sitter markdown rendering path never emitting [OSC 8 hyperlink escape sequences](https://gist.github.com/egmontkob/eb114294efbcd5adb1944c9f3cb5feda)** at all. The `<code filetype="markdown">` path (which is the default rendering path) parses markdown via tree-sitter and produces styled text chunks, but never sets the `link` property on those chunks — so the underlying terminal framework (opentui) has no URL to emit in OSC 8 sequences, regardless of whether the terminal supports them.

The fix involves:
1. **opentui side** ([anomalyco/opentui#736](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/736)): Adding an `onChunks` hook to `CodeRenderable` + exporting a `detectLinks()` helper, plus fixing the renderer to properly emit OSC 8 `id` parameters and re-emit sequences at row boundaries for wrapped links.
2. **opencode side**: Passing `onChunks={detectLinks}` to the `<code>` element in the session view so that URLs detected by tree-sitter get their `link` property set.

Once opentui merges and releases #736, the opencode change is a one-liner.

   ```bash
   bun uninstall -g opencode-ai
   ```

   ```bash
   bun install -g opencode-ai@1.2.10
   ```
